newsitem.title: EGYPT: Exceptional demand for Egyptian mill shares.
newsitem.headline: Exceptional demand for Egyptian mill shares.

text.p: The Egyptian state's privatisation offer of at least 2.4 million shares, or 40 percent of the equity, in East Delta Flour Mills drew exceptional demand, the agents said on Wednesday.
Mohamed el-Sharnoubi of agents Banque Misr said preliminary estimates were that 198,000 applications arrived for a total of some 58 million shares at the fixed price of 31 pounds a share.
"The problem is the number of individual investors, which is unprecedented compared to all former privatisations," he said. "This happened although we gave only 24 hours notice."
Individual investors have been allocated 1.2 million shares. This amount can be increased if demand justifies.
Mutual funds and financial institutions can buy 600,000 shares. The miller's employees are allocated the traditional portion of 10 percent.
The two-day flotation started on September 22.
The state regards milling firms as strategic and once said it would not sell more than 40 percent of its stake in them.
But heavy demand for an earlier privatisation, Central and West Delta Flour Mills, persuaded it to change its mind in that case.
